SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-15: FHIRPath — §6.3 Types. Test these items: is type specifier, is(type), as type specifier, as(type). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.evidence: Fresh probe .temp/qa/fp15_skeptic_probe.py: native and forced Python fallback returned (False, True) for `1 is System.Any`, `true is System.Any`, `Patient is System.Any`, and returned empty/false for `1.as(System.Any).exists()` / `Patient.as(System.Any).exists()`. Spec defines System.Any as the ultimate root/base type and §6.3 as/as returns the value for the requested type or subclass.
issues.root_cause: Both native fn_isType() and Python fallback TypeInfo/as_fn paths validated Any but never treated it as the root/base type before ordinary namespace/type comparisons.
issues.resolution: Added System/FHIR/unqualified Any root handling for is/as in native C++ and Python fallback; as(System.Any) now preserves singleton input across literals, FHIR resources, primitives, and complex values.
issues.verified_in: .temp/qa/fp15_skeptic_probe_after_fix.log; pytest test_type_parity.py 11 passed; native sqllogictest 594 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822

issues.evidence: Fresh probe .temp/qa/fp15_skeptic_probe.py: native returned (True, True) for `value.as(Integer).exists()` on Observation.valueInteger, while forced Python fallback returned (False, True). Direct `value.as(Integer)` was rescued by a wrapper shortcut, but the chained typed assertion fell through to core fallback exact namespace comparison.
issues.root_cause: The Python fallback type assertion path lost whether a capitalized primitive type specifier was explicitly System-qualified, and model-backed choice nodes carried only the resolved primitive type path, so chained value.as(Integer) used exact FHIR-vs-System namespace mismatch.
issues.resolution: Preserved explicit namespace metadata on TypeSpecifier values and added a choice-node guard for unqualified capitalized primitive choice assertions while keeping explicit System.Integer and ordinary primitive fields non-matching.
